services.desc: Yosemite Through Three Lenses features nineteenth-century mammoth prints, stereoviews, and cabinet cards by three pioneers of California landscape photography: Eadweard Muybridge, George Fiske, and Carleton Watkins. Of the three photographers, Muybridge was the most inventive; to him, the expansive Yosemite landscape presented a technical challenge to overcome. Watkins was the businessman; he understood the commercial value of images of Yosemite. Fiske was the romantic; he devoted his life to exploring and capturing the unique beauty of the region he called home.
